title: issue62424/fix62607 DDL implicit commit leaves stale transaction state trusted by GC

payload.validation_scope: deterministic upstream integration replay with -tags=intest: hold ADD INDEX after DDL enters queue, create a later active transaction, call ReportMinStartTS, and assert the reported minStartTS is the later active transaction rather than the stale DDL session startTS
payload.user_symptom: BEGIN followed by CREATE/ALTER INDEX can make GC believe an old transaction is still active, so GC safepoint progress is blocked while the DDL is running
payload.next_step: lift the same oracle to the authorized testbed by observing live GC safepoint or minStartTS while a long DDL issued inside a transaction is held in queue

name: GC minStartTS observer over DDL session state

state_model: session.SetProcessInfo writes ProcessInfo.CurTxnStartTS from SessionVars.TxnCtx.StartTS for running statements and in-transaction sessions
DDL execution calls sessiontxn.NewTxnInStmt and enqueues a DDL job; once the DDL job is in storage queue, StmtCtx.IsDDLJobInQueue is true
InfoSyncer.ReportMinStartTS reads SessionManager.ShowProcessList and uses each ProcessInfo.CurTxnStartTS to compute this server's minStartTS
GC worker consumes reported minStartTS to avoid advancing safepoint past active readers/transactions
fix 62607 skips processlist entries whose StmtCtx.IsDDLJobInQueue is true, so DDL sessions do not pin minStartTS after implicit commit
side_effects: DDL implicit commit clears the user transaction contract but not necessarily the processlist-visible CurTxnStartTS during statement execution
long DDL stays visible in processlist while the job is queued/executing
minStartTS can be pinned to a stale transaction startTS and delay GC progress
harness_capabilities: testkit can create mock store/domain and call dom.InfoSyncer().ReportMinStartTS(store,nil) directly
DDL mockDMLExecution/failpoint can hold ALTER TABLE ADD INDEX after the job is queued
a second real transaction can provide the expected active minStartTS control
upstream TestDDLInsideTXNNotBlockMinStartTS is a deterministic root-boundary oracle

name: DDL queued session must not pin GC minStartTS after implicit commit

payload.p_check: ReportMinStartTS sees a processlist entry with CurTxnStartTS and assumes it represents an active transaction or detached reader that GC must protect.
payload.q_claim: A DDL statement that has already been enqueued after implicit commit is no longer an active user transaction, so its stale CurTxnStartTS must not lower the reported minStartTS.

boundary.before: session begins a transaction, then executes ALTER/CREATE INDEX; DDL performs implicit commit and the DDL job enters the storage queue
boundary.fault: ProcessInfo.CurTxnStartTS from the pre-DDL transaction remains visible while StmtCtx.IsDDLJobInQueue is true
boundary.after: InfoSyncer.ReportMinStartTS scans ShowProcessList and chooses the minimum startTS to report for GC

fix 62607 integration test holds ADD INDEX and expects minStartTS to be the second active transaction's startTS, not the DDL session's older startTS
side_effects: GC safepoint progress is artificially delayed

a long DDL can make cluster GC appear blocked
consumers: long DDL jobs executed inside transaction context
payload.consequence: GC can be pinned by a stale DDL session startTS even though no user transaction needs that timestamp; this is an availability/space-retention correctness bug
payload.experiment_need: hold a DDL job after it enters queue, create a later active transaction as control, call ReportMinStartTS, and assert the reported minStartTS equals the active transaction startTS rather than the older DDL session startTS

name: GC minStartTS ignores queued DDL session startTS

payload.contract: When a DDL statement has already been enqueued after implicit commit, its processlist CurTxnStartTS must not be used as this server's reported minStartTS; the report must be governed by real active transactions/readers.
minimal_observation: start a transaction on the DDL session and record ddlTs
execute ADD INDEX in that session and hold it after the DDL job enters queue
start a second transaction and record tkTs where tkTs > ddlTs
call InfoSyncer.ReportMinStartTS while DDL is held
RED if GetMinStartTS never becomes tkTs because the stale DDL session startTS still pins the report
GREEN if GetMinStartTS becomes tkTs because queued DDL processlist entries are ignored
blind_spots: Does not directly observe the cluster GC safepoint advancing on a live deployment
Does not prove every DDL statement type; the replay uses ADD INDEX as a long-running representative
reusable_for: processlist fields consumed by background subsystems
GC/minStartTS observers that infer liveness from session state

rationale: the verified oracle is the narrow minStartTS boundary proven by issue62424

source_anchors: pkg/domain/infosync/info.go ReportMinStartTS uses ProcessInfo.CurTxnStartTS without skipping queued DDL sessions
pkg/session/session.go SetProcessInfo exposes SessionVars.TxnCtx.StartTS through CurTxnStartTS
pkg/ddl/executor.go marks StmtCtx.IsDDLJobInQueue after DDL job submission

evidence.oracle: while ADD INDEX is queued after implicit commit, ReportMinStartTS should ignore the DDL session's stale CurTxnStartTS and report the later active transaction startTS
evidence.red_observation: GetMinStartTS never reached tkTs within the Eventually window, showing the stale DDL session startTS still pinned minStartTS

lessons.selector_worked: IMPLICIT_COMMIT_STATE_CLEANUP became executable after asking which background observer trusts transaction state after DDL implicit commit.
lessons.method_note: The source proof obligation is P: processlist CurTxnStartTS exists; Q: it denotes an active transaction; F: queued DDL after implicit commit still carries stale CurTxnStartTS.
lessons.review_vs_test: Source review can identify the stale-state trust edge, but the test oracle makes it binary by comparing ddlTs with an independent tkTs control.
